meta.title: TherapyFarsi | Online counselling and therapy in Persian across Europe
meta.description: Online counselling and psychotherapy in Persian for Iranians and Persian speakers living in Europe and the UK, with experienced counsellors who know life as an immigrant.

home.heroLede: Online counselling and psychotherapy in Persian for Iranians and Persian speakers living in Europe, with experienced counsellors who know your language, your culture and the hard parts of life as an immigrant.
home.heroStatus: The first sessions open soon. We are finishing the last steps so everything works from day one.
home.archLabel: A window shaped like a Persian arch, looking out on a European city at dusk

why.title: The language of feelings
why.text: Some things only come out right in your mother tongue. Here you don’t search for words or cut your story short.

why.title: Someone who gets migration
why.text: Our counsellors know life in Europe: residence and work, family far away, a new language, and the feeling of standing between two places.

why.title: On your evening
why.text: Times are shown in your local time and sessions are online, from your own home, after work.

topics.title: Homesickness and migration grief
topics.text: Being far from family, missing the good and bad days of people you love, and feeling a stranger in a new country.

topics.title: Loneliness
topics.text: When there are people around you, but nobody you can really talk to.

topics.title: Anxiety and worry
topics.text: Racing thoughts about the future, constant unease, and sometimes panic attacks.

topics.title: Low mood and depression
topics.text: When nothing makes you happy, you have no energy, and the days just pass.

topics.title: Relationships and family
topics.text: Tension with a partner abroad, or pressure from family back home. Sessions are one-to-one.

topics.title: Work, study and visa pressure
topics.text: Burnout, visa and residence stress, and finding your feet in a new place.

topics.title: Between two cultures
topics.text: The feeling that you don’t fully belong there, or here.

topics.title: Sleep and mental exhaustion
topics.text: A mind that won’t switch off at night, and tiredness that rest doesn’t fix.

home.topicsNote: If your topic isn’t on this list, that’s fine. Start from where you are.

steps.title: Choose your counsellor
steps.text: Answer a few short questions to see counsellors who work with your topic, or browse the list yourself.

steps.title: Book a time
steps.text: Times are in your local time. You pay by international card and the receipt arrives by email.

steps.title: Talk from home
steps.text: The video session runs right here on the site. If your connection gets weak, carry on with audio only.

trust.title: Sessions are not recorded
trust.text: Each session link opens only for you and your counsellor, and no audio or video is stored.

trust.title: What you say stays with us
trust.text: Only the counsellor of that session sees your answers. Emails and messages never contain what you shared.

trust.title: A clear cancellation policy
trust.text: Cancel up to 24 hours before a session for a full refund, or move it to another time.

home.emergencyStrong: TherapyFarsi is not an emergency service.
home.emergencyText: If you are in immediate danger, call the emergency number of the country you are in right now: 112 in Europe, 999 in the UK. In the UK, call 111 for urgent help that isn’t an emergency.

faq.q: When can I book my first session?
faq.a: Soon. We are testing the site with a few counsellors and first clients so booking, payment and sessions work smoothly from day one.

Experienced Persian-speaking psychologists and counsellors who know life in Europe and the worries that come with migration. Some live in Europe themselves and some in Iran; each counsellor’s location is shown on their own page. Their identity and professional credentials are checked before they join.
Yes. Sessions are not recorded and audio and video travel encrypted. Questionnaire answers are stored encrypted and only the counsellor of that session can read them.

faq.q: What if I don’t click with my counsellor after the first session?
faq.a: A good fit with your counsellor matters more than anything. If it doesn’t feel right, support will help you book your next session with another counsellor who suits you better.

faq.q: Which countries can I use it from?
faq.a: We focus on Iranians and Persian speakers living in Europe and the UK. Session times are shown in your local time.
No. Sessions are talk-based: counselling and psychotherapy. If medication may help, your counsellor will help you see a doctor in the country where you live.

faq.q: What if the internet drops during a session?
faq.a: You can carry on with audio only. If a session is cut short by a connection problem, you can move it for free or get your money back.

faq.q: How much does it cost and how do I pay?
faq.a: Each counsellor’s page shows the price of a 50-minute session in euros or pounds. You pay by bank card, Apple Pay or Google Pay.

home.footerTagline: Online counselling and psychotherapy in Persian
home.contactText: Message us on WhatsApp about the site, when sessions start, or joining as a counsellor. Please don’t write your personal history or what you want to work on; that belongs in a session.
home.whyLead: Even if your English or German is excellent, your sorrows speak Persian.
home.whyBody: When you feel low or your head is full, the last thing you want is to hunt for words in another language, or spend an hour explaining to a non-Iranian counsellor how an Iranian family works, what “taarof” means, and why, from this far away, your family’s worries still sit on your shoulders.
storyBody: Migration isn’t only a change of map; sometimes it means losing a piece of yourself in a new country. TherapyFarsi started from that experience.

We know the Sunday-evening homesickness in Europe, being stuck between staying and going back, and how hard it is to say your deepest pain in a second language. We want a place where you can talk without censoring yourself, without fear of judgement, in your mother tongue, with someone who understands you.

callTest.title: Call test
callTest.intro: This is a temporary page for measuring call quality from Iran. Calls are not recorded and nothing is stored on the server.
callTest.roomHint: Lowercase English letters, digits and dashes only, 3–40 characters. Both people must type the same name.
callTest.name: Your name
callTest.forceRelay: Force TURN over port 443 (tests networks that block UDP)
callTest.leaveHint: To end the call, press the leave button inside the call. The report is built after that.
callTest.reportHint: Rate the call, copy the report and send it to the site owner.
